title: Identifiability through GPS and timestamp data
description: The wearable device captures GPS position and timestamps, which can be used to identify the wearer's location patterns, movements, and routines. This sensitive location data combined with timestamps creates a detailed profile that can uniquely identify the individual.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted or stored in a way that preserves location precision; timestamps are retained and accessible.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location data
description: Heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps constitute sensitive personal data. If the wearable device is compromised, data is transmitted insecurely, or unauthorized access occurs, this data could be disclosed to third parties without consent.
assumptions: Device security is not perfect; data transmission may not be end-to-end encrypted; unauthorized access vectors exist.

title: Linkability of sensor data to other data sources
description: The sensor telemetry data (heart rate, GPS, timestamps) can potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., social media, other devices, third-party services) to create a comprehensive profile of the wearer's behavior, health status, and location history.
assumptions: Data sharing or integration with external systems occurs; data formats allow correlation across sources.

title: Excessive data collection beyond necessity
description: The device continuously captures multiple types of sensor data (heart rate, steps, GPS, timestamps) which may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose. Continuous GPS tracking and health monitoring may be more invasive than required for basic device functionality.
assumptions: Data collection scope is not minimized; continuous monitoring is enabled by default.

title: Linkability of GPS traces and timestamps across sessions
description: GPS traces combined with timestamps and device ID can be linked to identify specific user movements and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive location history that could be correlated with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is retained and accessible for correlation analysis
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability threats

title: Identifiability through device ID and location data
description: Device ID combined with GPS traces and timestamps can uniquely identify the user, especially when correlated with other data sources or when the device is not anonymized.
assumptions: Device ID is not properly anonymized or pseudonymized
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability threats

title: Implicit data disclosure through metadata
description: Metadata such as timestamps, GPS coordinates, and device ID may reveal more information than intended, including user routines, frequent locations, and behavioral patterns that could be disclosed to third parties.
assumptions: Metadata is not stripped or minimized before transmission
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data disclosure threats

title: Usurpation of location data for unauthorized tracking
description: GPS traces and timestamps could be misused for unauthorized tracking purposes, such as stalking, insurance fraud, or employment monitoring without user consent.
assumptions: Data is accessible to unauthorized parties or used beyond intended purpose
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for usurpation threats

title: Data integrity compromise during sensor data transmission
description: Sensor data including exercise sessions and GPS traces could be tampered with during transmission, leading to inaccurate health records or fraudulent activity claims.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not adequately secured or authenticated
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data integrity threats

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: The companion mobile app (P2) may disclose the user's calorie, meal, and weight data to unauthorized third parties, violating privacy expectations for sensitive health information.
assumptions: The app may share data with third-party services, advertisers, or cloud providers without explicit user consent.

title: User unawareness of data usage
description: The user (EE1) may be unaware of how their personal health data is being collected, stored, processed, or shared by the companion app, including potential secondary uses beyond the stated purpose.
assumptions: Privacy policies may be complex or users may not read them; data may be shared with third parties without clear notification.

title: Data falsification by user
description: The user (EE1) may intentionally falsify calorie, meal, or weight entries in the companion app, leading to inaccurate health data that could mislead health tracking or medical decisions.
assumptions: Users may have motivation to underreport calories or overreport weight for personal or social reasons.

title: Explicit Health Data Disclosure to DataStore
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) explicitly transfers personal health data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to the Health Log Store (DS1) as part of its designed functionality. This constitutes an explicit data disclosure where personal data crosses the process-to-datastore boundary.
assumptions: Health logs contain personally identifiable health information that could be used to identify or profile individuals.
uncertainty_note: This is the intended design of the system, so the disclosure is by design. The threat is about whether this disclosure is avoidable or if additional safeguards are needed.

title: Linkability of Health Log Entries to Individuals
description: Health log data (weight history, exercise sessions, calorie intake) written to the store could be linked to specific individuals, potentially enabling identification or re-identification of users through their health patterns and behavioral data.
assumptions: Health data is inherently personal and can be associated with specific users through account credentials or device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the data is stored with user identifiers or can be linked through the app's authentication system.

title: Inference of Sensitive Health Information from Log Data
description: Analysis of stored health logs (weight trends, exercise patterns, calorie intake) could allow inference of sensitive health conditions, lifestyle habits, or medical information beyond what was explicitly recorded.
assumptions: Patterns in health data can reveal underlying health conditions, fitness levels, dietary restrictions, or other sensitive personal information.
uncertainty_note: Inference depends on the sophistication of data analysis and the completeness of the health log data.

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Health Data Storage
description: Storing health-related personal data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) may trigger regulatory requirements under HIPAA, GDPR, or other health data protection regulations, requiring specific safeguards and consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Health data is classified as sensitive personal data subject to strict regulatory frameworks.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific data classification policies.

title: Explicit Location Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: GPS location traces with timestamps written to the location history store may be accessible to unauthorized third parties, violating the minimality principle. Location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly necessary.
assumptions: The location history store may have access controls that are insufficient, or the data may be shared with third-party services without explicit consent.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the store architecture allows third-party access; would need to verify actual access controls.

title: Linkability of Location Traces to User Identity
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be linked across multiple data points to reconstruct detailed movement patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about user habits, routines, and locations visited.
assumptions: Location data is stored in a format that allows correlation across time periods.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the data is stored in a way that enables temporal correlation.

title: Identifiability of Location Data to Specific Individual
description: GPS location traces are inherently identifiable as they track movements of a specific device/user. Even without explicit identifiers, the unique pattern of location data can be used to identify the individual.
assumptions: The location data is not anonymized or aggregated before storage.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the data is stored at individual device level rather than aggregated.

title: Location Data Integrity Compromise
description: GPS location traces written to the location history store could be altered, deleted, or tampered with by unauthorized actors, potentially leading to false location records or denial of service.
assumptions: The data store lacks adequate integrity controls or authentication mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the store may not have robust integrity verification.

assumptions: The analytics service has legitimate access to health data for analysis purposes

title: Identifiability Through Location History
description: Location history data can directly identify individuals by revealing their movements, locations, and routines. Even without explicit identifiers, the pattern of movements can be used to infer individual identity when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals' movements and routines.

assumptions: Analytics service has access to sufficient historical health data to identify group-level patterns; insights may be shared or stored in ways that enable cross-referencing.
